labctl.notes: x11 runtime (MAME indy_4610, -video none + shm capture); no QMP; input = streamhost mamesock -> mamectl OSD module unix socket ctl.sock (pointer + keys; rollback SH_INPUT_BACKEND=mamecmd + module file tail, deep rollback IRIX_CTL=off = Lua agent); exec = serial_e — irixser/2 over MAME -ioc2:rs232a pty to irixagent.pl baked into the golden, host client /root/irixexec.py, no port; reset = relaunch

museum.blurb: SGI’s 1993 Indy brought real workstation Unix — 64-bit MIPS, hardware 24-bit graphics, and the gorgeous teal Indigo Magic Desktop — to a friendly blue pizza-box. IRIX 6.5 was the definitive SGI Unix, booting to the 4Dwm desktop.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile — the FIRST non-QEMU tile: an Xvfb + MAME(indy_4610) emulator captured directly by streamhost’s SH_CAPTURE=shm backend (MAME’s SGI Indy emulation kernel-panics under a KVM vCPU, so it runs on the bare-metal CPU, not a QEMU VM). archetype beige-tower-crt. See docs/history/irix-tile-issue20-handoff.md.

reset.fixture: SGI Indy (MIPS R4600 100MHz) IRIX 6.5 4Dwm Indigo Magic desktop in MAME indy_4610; xl24 24-bit graphics, exact emulated framebuffer 1288x1024; captured via streamhost SH_CAPTURE=shm (MAME -video none, no X server) + mamesock ioport input (mamectl ctl.sock, issue #45). x11-runtime (Xvfb/MAME) tile added 2026-07-30 (issue #20).
